title: Breakthroughs change the limiting step
scope: Ten selected explanatory routes through an existing longer history, not a complete causal history or a claim that progress follows one inevitable path.

timelinePreservation.policy: Add a guided route; do not replace, deduplicate, reorder or shorten the original combined timeline.
timelinePreservation.matching: year + exact title + component + source URL

steps.title: Control a channel with an insulated electrode

milestone.title: Kahng files an insulated-gate field-effect device patent

steps.breakthrough: Kahng filed the cited insulated-field circuit patent in 1960; this is a specific filing milestone, not a sole-inventor claim for all modern transistors.
steps.mechanism: An insulated electrode changes the electric field and surface charge. Gate capacitance connects voltage control to charge and energy.

result.basis: Ideal fixed capacitor, not transistor current, leakage or a historic device measurement.

experience.question: At fixed capacitance, what happens to stored energy when gate voltage doubles?
experience.basis: Authored worked arithmetic with explicit assumptions; the historical source supports the mechanism, not these invented inputs.

changedBottleneck.relieved: Control of semiconductor conduction without a conducting gate connection.
changedBottleneck.remaining: Interface quality, leakage, electrostatics and fabrication variability still constrain a usable switch.

steps.title: Make connections a designed part of the chip
steps.breakthrough: The 1997 integrated-copper report connected materials and fabrication changes to a usable multilevel wiring process.
steps.mechanism: Wire resistance and capacitance impose a timescale even after transistor switching becomes fast.

result.basis: Synthetic uniform wire; lumped R×C timescale excludes distributed geometry, drivers, vias, size effects and coupling.

experience.question: Why does doubling length quadruple this uniform-wire RC timescale?
experience.basis: Authored worked arithmetic with explicit assumptions; the historical source supports the mechanism, not these invented inputs.

changedBottleneck.relieved: The wiring material/process can lower resistance at a specified geometry.
changedBottleneck.remaining: Vias, dielectric coupling, routing congestion, reliability and driver behavior remain.

steps.title: Express a workload as many programmable threads

milestone.title: CUDA opens GPU execution to general computation

steps.breakthrough: CUDA introduced a way to program GPU computation outside graphics APIs in 2006.
steps.mechanism: Map independent output work to logical threads; instruction grouping and inactive lanes determine which issued work is useful.

result.basis: Exact small integer result. Inspect R21 architecture-execution for synthetic scalar/vector/SIMT/systolic schedules; no vendor timing is inferred.

experience.question: Which output/partial product is assigned to each active SIMT lane?
experience.basis: Authored worked arithmetic with explicit assumptions; the historical source supports the mechanism, not these invented inputs.

changedBottleneck.relieved: General workload expression can exploit parallel arithmetic hardware.
changedBottleneck.remaining: Memory movement, inactive lanes, synchronization and software mapping can limit throughput.

steps.title: Place logic and memory on dense package routes
steps.breakthrough: TSMC dates CoWoS volume production to 2012.
steps.mechanism: An interposer connects logic and stacked memory through many short parallel routes; width and signaling rate together determine a link budget.

result.basis: Synthetic independent lanes at an assumed sustained payload fraction, not a CoWoS or HBM specification.

experience.question: At the same lane rate and payload fraction, how does 64 versus 256 lanes change the byte-rate budget?
experience.basis: Authored worked arithmetic with explicit assumptions; the historical source supports the mechanism, not these invented inputs.

changedBottleneck.relieved: Package routing supports wider memory interfaces than a narrow off-package route.
changedBottleneck.remaining: HBM supply, known-good die, assembly/test capacity, signal integrity and heat now matter together.

steps.title: Use gradient history when updating parameters

milestone.title: Adam combines momentum with adaptive scaling

steps.breakthrough: Adam was first submitted in 2014 as a stochastic optimization method.
steps.mechanism: Track first and second gradient moments, correct their initialization bias and scale each parameter update.

result.basis: Authored scalar gradients demonstrate Adam moments and bias correction; not training loss, convergence evidence or the SGD classifier used in R26.

experience.question: Why does the first second-moment estimate need a bias correction before it scales the update?
experience.basis: Authored worked arithmetic with explicit assumptions; the historical source supports the mechanism, not these invented inputs.

changedBottleneck.relieved: Per-parameter adaptive scaling can change optimization behavior.
changedBottleneck.remaining: Extra optimizer state consumes memory; progress still depends on data, objective and evaluation.

steps.title: Weight values by query–key compatibility
steps.breakthrough: The 2017 Transformer paper presented an attention-based sequence architecture.
steps.mechanism: Scaled query–key dot products become softmax weights over values; this creates structured matrix and memory work.

result.basis: Scalar one-row online softmax illustrates rescaling and unchanged output. It is not a complete FlashAttention kernel or measured HBM traffic; Q/K/V, state, output and hardware storage are excluded from temporary-score counts.

experience.question: With scores 1/√2 and 0, why is the weighted value between 10 and 20?
experience.basis: Authored worked arithmetic with explicit assumptions; the historical source supports the mechanism, not these invented inputs.

changedBottleneck.relieved: Attention supports content-dependent mixing across sequence positions.
changedBottleneck.remaining: Dense pair interactions, activation storage, data quality and evaluation remain constraints.

steps.title: Move operands through a matrix datapath
steps.breakthrough: The first TPU architecture paper appeared in 2017 and described an accelerator already deployed since 2015.
steps.mechanism: A matrix datapath reuses operands across processing elements; data arrival and fill/drain behavior determine useful activity.

result.basis: Exact small integer result. Inspect R21 architecture-execution for synthetic scalar/vector/SIMT/systolic schedules; no vendor timing is inferred.

experience.question: How can neighboring processing elements share operands while preserving exactly the same output?
experience.basis: Authored worked arithmetic with explicit assumptions; the historical source supports the mechanism, not these invented inputs. The R21 output-stationary array is a different dataflow from the weight-stationary TPU described in this paper.

changedBottleneck.relieved: Structured matrix work can reuse local data and amortize control.
changedBottleneck.remaining: Array shape, padding, memory supply and workload compatibility still limit utilization.

steps.title: Preserve the result while changing data movement
steps.breakthrough: FlashAttention introduced an IO-aware exact-attention algorithm in 2022.
steps.mechanism: Tile inputs and update softmax statistics online so a full attention-score matrix need not be materialized in HBM.

result.basis: Scalar one-row online softmax illustrates rescaling and unchanged output. It is not a complete FlashAttention kernel or measured HBM traffic; Q/K/V, state, output and hardware storage are excluded from temporary-score counts.

experience.question: When the running maximum changes, why must old numerator and denominator be rescaled together?
experience.basis: Authored worked arithmetic with explicit assumptions; the historical source supports the mechanism, not these invented inputs.

changedBottleneck.relieved: Avoidable attention-score materialization and transfers can be reduced.
changedBottleneck.remaining: Compute, on-chip storage, tile boundaries and other layer traffic still constrain execution.

steps.title: Allocate live KV state in blocks
steps.breakthrough: PagedAttention was published in 2023 with a block-based KV-cache management design.
steps.mechanism: A request maps logical token blocks to physical allocations instead of reserving a large contiguous maximum-sized region.

result.basis: Synthetic token-slot allocation with fixed-size blocks; no sharing, metadata cost, quantization, multiple layers, scheduler or physical token-byte claim. A negative saving is possible under a different reservation convention.

experience.question: Why do 14 live token slots require 20 block-allocated slots here, and how does that compare with 24 reserved slots?
experience.basis: Authored worked arithmetic with explicit assumptions; the historical source supports the mechanism, not these invented inputs.

changedBottleneck.relieved: A block allocation policy can reduce unused reserved KV space.
changedBottleneck.remaining: Block metadata, fragmentation within the final block, bandwidth, batching and latency remain.

steps.title: Integrate compute, fabric, power and cooling
steps.breakthrough: The 2024 GB200 NVL72 announcement illustrates rack integration of compute trays, scale-up switching and liquid cooling.
steps.mechanism: Installed hardware supplies useful work only when electrical, cooling, fabric and operational requirements align.

result.basis: Synthetic simultaneous admission of whole-rack jobs. PUE is a fixed scenario conversion factor, not a measured site value; all allocated IT power becomes heat. No network/memory compatibility, topology, priorities, job duration or wait times are modeled.

rows.reason: Entire request does not fit remaining racks.

result.scope: First-fit skips an oversized waiting request; strict-order stops admitting subsequent requests. Neither is asserted to be an actual public-computing or commercial scheduler policy.

experience.question: Which condition limits admitted racks, and why can installed racks exceed concurrent useful capacity?
experience.basis: Authored worked arithmetic with explicit assumptions; the historical source supports the mechanism, not these invented inputs.

changedBottleneck.relieved: Rack-level integration coordinates repeated compute and communication components.
changedBottleneck.remaining: Site readiness, compatible resources, heat rejection, admission policy and recovery can become limiting.
